content.thinking:
Member removal requires admin privileges. Issue assignment requires a member.

Admins can assign issues via role. Unassigning all issues when one fails requires a rollback.

Using assignIssue centralizes event emission. It safely handles null assignees and publishes issue.unassigned when clearing an assignee. A circular import risk exists if issue-service later imports member-service, but member-service importing issue-service is safe. Alternatively, issue-service could expose a dedicated unassignment function for member-service to call.

A dedicated function is cleaner than embedding the loop inside removeMember. The member must be archived before unassigning issues, or the member will remain active and the unassignment may fail. The requirement is to unassign every live issue assigned to the removed member.

Unassignment will run after the member is archived. If it fails, the member is already removed. Both events should still fire. Unassigning issues before emitting member.removed keeps the transaction logically consistent. No transaction wrapper exists.
